title: 3D Soft-Body Collision and Deformation Simulation
prompt:
Implement a 3D soft-body simulation using Three.js: two deformable elastic spheres fall onto the ground under gravity and collide with each other.

[Three.js Import Method (Must Be Followed Strictly)]
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>

[Soft-Body Model (Mass-Spring Tetrahedral Mesh)]

Each elastic sphere consists of a tetrahedral mesh:
- Use THREE.IcosahedronGeometry(1.0, 2) as the surface mesh (162 vertices)
- Add an additional central mass point (centroid)
- Connect the central mass point to every surface vertex with springs (radial springs)
- Connect adjacent surface vertices with springs (surface springs)

Spring parameters:
- Stiffness k = 500 N/m (radial springs)
- Stiffness k = 300 N/m (surface springs)
- Damping d = 5.8
- restLength = the original distance between the two endpoints at creation time

Each vertex/mass point:
- mass = 0.01 kg
- Position + velocity state

Integration: Verlet Integration, dt = 0.002s
  x_new = 2*x - x_prev + acceleration * dt²
  5 substeps per frame

Initial positions of the two spheres:
- Sphere A: center at (-1.5, 5, 0), red
- Sphere B: center at (1.5, 6, 0), blue

Collision detection and response:
1. Ground collision (y=0): if a vertex has y < 0, set y = 0, vy = -vy * 0.3
2. Sphere-sphere collision: for every vertex of sphere A and every vertex of sphere B, if the distance < 0.1, apply mutually repulsive spring forces
   F = k_contact * (0.1 - dist) * direction, k_contact = 1000

Pressure maintenance (volume-conservation approximation):
- Each frame, calculate the current volume of each sphere (approximated using the cube of the average distance from the center to the surface: V ≈ 4/3 π r_avg³)
- If the volume < original volume * 0.7, apply an outward expansion force to all surface vertices
  F_pressure = pressure_coeff * (V0 - V) / V0 * outward_normal
  pressure_coeff = 200

[Rendering]
(1) Two elastic spheres: each is a THREE.Mesh; update vertex positions and recompute normals every frame
(2) Sphere A is red and semi-transparent (opacity=0.7); sphere B is blue and semi-transparent
(3) Ground: gray grid
(4) The internal spring network can be seen: mark the center point with a small sphere and draw radial springs with thin lines (optional toggle)
(5) OrbitControls

[HUD and Controls]
(6) HUD:
  - Sphere A center-of-mass position (id="posA")
  - Sphere B center-of-mass position (id="posB")
  - Sphere A current volume/original volume ratio (id="volRatioA")
  - Sphere B current volume/original volume ratio (id="volRatioB")
  - Simulation time (id="simTime")

(7) Reset button (id="resetBtn")
(8) Apply impulse button (id="pushBtn"): apply a rightward impulse to sphere A so that the two spheres collide

[State Exposure]
window.__3D_STATE__:
  - simTime: simulation time
  - bodyA: { center:{x,y,z}, avgRadius, volumeRatio, speed, nodeCount, nodes(25 sampled):[{x,y,z}] }
  - bodyB: { center:{x,y,z}, avgRadius, volumeRatio, speed, nodeCount, nodes(25 sampled):[{x,y,z}] }
  - totalEnergy: total energy (spring potential energy + kinetic energy + gravitational potential energy)
  - groundContacts: number of vertices in contact with the ground (combined total for both spheres)

Output a single standalone HTML file.
